label: UniFi LTE Backup Pro
description: UniFi LTE Backup Pro - a failover modem for a UniFi gateway: two GbE RJ45 ports (one powered by PoE-in, one passing PoE through) and an LTE Cat 4 radio with an internal antenna pair plus an RP-SMA connector for an external one.
notes: Vendor figures from Ubiquiti techspecs: (2) GbE RJ45 ports - one PoE in, one PoE passthrough output requiring a PoE source - and an LTE Category 4 radio with (2) internal antennas and (1) female RP-SMA connector for an external antenna. Max power consumption 8.5 W excluding PoE passthrough. The LTE interface is modelled at 100M, the Cat 4 class shared with every other Cat 4 device in the catalogue, because the datasheet names the category rather than a measured rate.

label: UniFi Long-Range Ethernet Repeater
description: UniFi Long-Range Ethernet Repeater (UACC-LRE) - two GbE RJ45 ports that extend a run past the 100 m copper limit, with passthrough PoE so the downstream device is still powered from the source switch.
notes: Vendor figures from Ubiquiti techspecs: (2) GbE RJ45 ports with (1) passthrough PoE output, 2-pairs (pins 1,2+; 3,6-). It is a two-port inline repeater: no switch fabric, no radio, no management plane beyond link handling, so it is modelled as two ports rather than as a switch.

label: EdgeSwitch 5 XP
description: EdgeSwitch 5 XP (ES-5XP) - five gigabit RJ45 ports with PoE configurable per port, plus a separate 10/100 management port. The small PoE switch in the EdgeSwitch XP line.
notes: Vendor figures from Ubiquiti techspecs: (5) 10/100/1000 Ethernet ports and (1) 10/100 Ethernet port for management, so the management port is modelled at 100M and named separately from the five data ports. PoE is present on the data ports - the datasheet carries per-port wattage, method and 'PoE configurable per port' rows - but the standard (802.3af/at vs passive 24V) was not captured during intake, so no 802.3 capability is claimed. If your unit negotiates 802.3af, that is a gap worth a comment.
